A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SegMAN, with matching core methods and experiments. The text, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including identification of relocated material and inconsistent reported values.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet classification, semantic segmentation, inference-speed, and architectural ablation results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original SegMAN experiments and adds larger-model results, hyperparameter and component-transfer studies, and instance/panoptic segmentation results.

M1.justification: Table 1 adds a Large architecture with channels [96,192,432,640] and block counts [4,4,28,4]. This extends the model family, while the LASS operation, final-stage global attention, MMSCopE processing, and feature-fusion procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Supplementary Section D adds instance and panoptic segmentation using the SegMAN encoder within Mask DINO, substantially extending task coverage. The dataset for these experiments is not identified. ImageNet classification and semantic segmentation on ADE20K, Cityscapes, and COCO-Stuff remain covered.

E2.justification: ImageNet comparisons expand substantially to include InternImage, ViM, VMamba, SparX-Mamba, MaxViT, and MambaTree variants; PVT-S/M entries are replaced by PVTv2 variants in the detailed comparison. SegFormer-B5 and VWFormer-B5 join segmentation and speed comparisons. The new Mask DINO comparison evaluates ResNet50 and MiT-B2 against SegMAN-S.

E3.justification: v2 adds the Large model configuration and a Mask DINO evaluation using instance AP, panoptic PQ, and batch size 48, described relative to Mask DINO's default 16. Encoder-ablation complexity profiling changes from 224×224 in v1 Table 8 to 512×512 in v2 Table 5. Existing segmentation crops, 160K training iterations, and speed-measurement procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds window-size and SSM expansion/state-dimension ablations in Table 10 and extends component-transfer analysis with SegMAN decoders attached to SegNeXt and CGRSeg encoders in Table 12. It also expands encoder-ablation efficiency evidence and revises the scan-resolution/downsampling analysis. The feature-fusion study is retained unchanged, moving from v1 Table 7 to supplementary Table 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The 128-step averaging used for inference-speed measurement is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds SegMAN-L results of 53.2/84.2/48.8 mIoU across the three segmentation benchmarks, 85.5% ImageNet accuracy, and Mask DINO results of 49.6 AP and 56.8 PQ, alongside new baseline, runtime, and ablation entries. Tiny/Small/Base headline scores are retained. Table 9 replaces the 51.3 reference mIoU with 50.0 while also changing parameter/FLOP values, preventing interpretation as a demonstrated same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: The spatial-scale relations and mathematical reasoning about feature rearrangement remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract adds the claim that SegMAN-B Encoder achieves 85.1% ImageNet accuracy, outperforming VMamba-S by 1.5 points with fewer parameters, and the introduction foregrounds backbone competitiveness. Classification was already evaluated in v1; the central LASS, MMSCopE, and semantic-segmentation contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets component-substitution results as evidence of plug-and-play compatibility and independently useful encoders and decoders. Supplementary Section D extends the interpretation to task-agnostic applicability beyond semantic segmentation. Existing explanations of local/global complementarity and information preservation remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly states a learning rate of 1e-6 and 1500 warmup iterations, supplies Large-model and window/SSM configuration details, and revises reported training hardware from eight H100 GPUs to eight H800 GPUs. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unstated settings or experimental reruns. The code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, including Mask DINO, PVTv2, InternImage, SparX, and MambaTree. Related work acknowledges additional advanced vision backbones, but the existing segmentation-encoder, decoder, and Vision Mamba framing and central novelty positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Most methodological and experimental prose is retained, with localized abstract, introduction, experiment-description, and conclusion rewrites. Encoder and decoder ablation sections exchange order, the fusion analysis moves into supplementary material, and the appendix is reorganized into Sections A–E.

P2.justification: v2 adds a four-panel performance-versus-parameter overview, updates architecture-diagram labels, substantially repacks the benchmark tables, adds an FPS column to encoder ablations, and introduces several supplementary tables. Existing qualitative figures are retained and relocated to dedicated supplementary pages.

improvement.justification: Broader baselines, model scaling, and new transfer/task studies provide useful additional evidence, but v2 introduces unresolved inconsistencies. The SegMAN-S/HAM result remains 50.4 mIoU in Table 6, matching v1 Table 5, while new Table 12 reports 49.2 for the same named configuration and complexity without explaining different settings. Unexplained Table 9 revisions and the unspecified dataset for Mask DINO further limit interpretation. These issues prevent reliably weighing the expanded evidence against reduced internal consistency.
